key_insight: A BDF2-type finite element scheme for inertial magnetization dynamics is unconditionally stable and converges to a weak solution without coupling time-step and mesh sizes.
engineering_relevance: The method supports reliable simulation of subpicosecond magnetization dynamics relevant to ultrafast magnetic devices.
method: Use first-order finite elements in space and BDF2 time stepping.
Treat inertia with a convex combination of BDF2 and backward Euler.
Prove well-posedness, a discrete energy law, and explicit unit-length constraint error bounds.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments assess performance and validate the theoretical findings, but the abstract reports no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: Unconditional convergence does not guarantee accuracy at large time steps, and the unit-length constraint has a bounded discretization error.
paper_title: An unconditionally convergent BDF2-type finite element integrator for the inertial Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation
